Shape-Constrained Tensor Product Smooth of Two Covariates

Source: R/scte.R
scte.Rd

Constructs a smooth function of two covariates that is monotone in one of them for every value of the other, or monotone in both. The term enters the formula of any distribution parameter, like te().

Usage

scte(
  x,
  z,
  shapes = list(shape_increasing(), NULL),
  smooths = basis7::bspline_smooth(k = 6),
  by = NULL,
  by_hyper = c("shared", "level"),
  hyper = NULL,
  id = NULL,
  label = NULL
)

Arguments

x, z

The covariates, bare names or expressions in the data.

shapes

A list of two elements, for x and for z: each is shape_increasing(), shape_decreasing() or NULL for a free margin, and at least one is a shape. A shape here takes neither min_slope nor a value or a slope at a point.

smooths

A basis7 smoother whose basis is a B-spline, or a list of two, one per covariate: basis7::bspline_smooth() (the default, with six basis functions) or basis7::pspline_smooth(). Only the bases are used.

by

An optional factor or numeric variable, given as a bare name or an expression in the data, as in s().

by_hyper

With a factor by, whether the levels share the two smoothing parameters ("shared", the default) or each level has its own pair ("level").

hyper

NULL to estimate the smoothing parameters, or values at which to hold them, named lambda1 and lambda2 (with the level appended under by_hyper = "level", as lambda1.a).

id

NULL, or strings shared with other terms whose smoothing parameters are the same, named as hyper.

label

The term's label; NULL builds scte(<x>, <z>) from the call.

Value

An unbuilt ScteTerm.

The construction

Each covariate is expanded in the B-spline basis of its smoother, and the surface is \(f(x, z) = B_x(x)^\top \Theta B_z(z)\) with \(\Theta\) the \(K_x \times K_z\) matrix of the tensor-product coefficients. A margin with a shape writes its direction of \(\Theta\) as cumulative sums of increments on the Greville abscissae of its basis, as shape_increasing() does for one covariate, each increment constrained through the inverse of the log link. With the shape on \(x\) alone, \(\Theta = A_x B\): every column of \(\Theta\), a function of \(x\) at one coefficient of \(z\), is monotone, and the first row of \(B\) is a free function of \(z\) whose coefficients sum to zero, the constant being left to the intercept of the model. With shapes on both margins, \(\Theta = A_x B A_z^\top\) and every element of \(B\) except the level \(b_{11}\) is constrained. A decreasing margin is the increasing one in the reflected covariate, which reverses the order of its basis.

The interaction under two shapes

With shapes on both margins every increment is constrained, the cross increments \(b_{jk}\), \(j, k \ge 2\), included. The surface is then monotone in both covariates, and its interaction has a fixed sign: the mixed differences of \(\Theta\) are nonnegative when both margins are increasing or both decreasing, and nonpositive when one is increasing and the other decreasing. A surface that is increasing in both covariates with a negative interaction, such as \(x + z - xz/2\), is not of this form, and the fit is biased for it; with the shape on one margin the interaction is free. The construction is that of Pya and Wood (2015).

The penalty

Two smoothing parameters, lambda1 and lambda2, are selected with the rest of the model. lambda1 penalizes the first differences of the constrained coordinates of \(\gamma\) along \(x\), and lambda2 those along \(z\); the free row or column has the second differences of its coefficients along its own direction under the smoothing parameter of that direction.

Varying the surface by another variable

A factor by gives one surface per level, each with the shapes of shapes, and the level means come from the factor written in the formula; the coefficients are named <label>.<level>.g1, and so on. Under by_hyper = "level" each level has its own pair of smoothing parameters, named lambda1.<level> and lambda2.<level>. A numeric by \(w\) gives the varying-coefficient term \(w\,f(x, z)\): the level of \(f\) is then a free and unpenalized coefficient, <label>.const, and the default label is scte(x, z):w.

Prediction outside the data

Beyond the interval of a basis the surface is held at its value at the boundary, which preserves the shapes.

References

Pya, N. and Wood, S. N. (2015). Shape constrained additive models. Statistics and Computing, 25, 543–559.

See also

scs() for one covariate, te() for the unconstrained tensor product.

Examples

set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(x = runif(150), z = runif(150))
tm <- term_build(scte(x, z, shapes = list(shape_increasing(), NULL)), dd)
f <- term_value(tm, coef = rnorm(length(term_coef_names(tm))),
                newdata = expand.grid(x = seq(0, 1, 0.1), z = 0.3))
all(diff(f) >= -1e-12)
#> [1] TRUE

# Increasing in both covariates.
scte(x, z, shapes = list(shape_increasing(), shape_increasing()))
#> <ScteTerm> 'scte(x, z)' (specification; call term_build() with data); increasing in x, increasing in z
